title: Marketplace listing voice and quota guardrails - draft
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working draft for two tightly-coupled deliverables requested by channel and product teams:
  1) a tone-and-voice + short/long copy bundle for cloud marketplace tiles (AWS/Azure/GCP) optimized for enterprise customers; and
  2) an operational "quota & guardrails" checklist that defines listing-level usage limits, billing SKU equivalencies, and preflight acceptance criteria so integrations can ship with predictable cost/limits.

Audience:
- Partner PMs and partner engineering (to review guardrails)
- Marketplace ops (to validate SKU/billing mapping)
- GTM copywriters and CDN/localization teams
- Solutions engineers for pre-sales Q&A

Guiding constraints (must follow marketplace rules + Redwood positioning):
- Language must be concise, technical, and benefits-forward (latency, cost predictability, security).
- Avoid proprietary claims about model architectures; emphasize performance and SLAs instead.
- Keep the hero tile to ~300 characters, long description ~800–1,200 characters.
- Include explicit callouts for deployment modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) — abbreviated where space is tight.
- Provide an explicit SKU and feature matrix for marketplace billing teams.

Copy variants (pick the one that fits vendor character limits).
Short hero (<= 280 chars):
  Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM inference with predictable latency and cost. Ship hosted or private, choose dedicated capacity for guaranteed throughput. Built-in observability, canary rollouts, and enterprise controls.

Short variant (more product-y):
  Fast, reliable LLM inference for production apps. Hosted API or private deployments, reserved GPU capacity, and per-route observability to keep latency and cost predictable.

Long description (800–1,000 chars):
  Redwood Inference makes it straightforward to run large language models in production without rebuilding the serving stack. Use our hosted API for quickest time-to-value, reserve Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, or deploy Private for VPC/on-prem workloads and compliance controls. The platform optimizes throughput and token cost via dynamic batching, KV/prefix caching, and model-aware quantization. Teams get per-route dashboards (latency, cost per token), rollout controls (canary, A/B, auto-fallback), and integration hooks for key management and audit logging. Backed by SLAs for uptime and latency targets, Redwood is designed for engineering teams building LLM features that must scale, stay cost-effective, and meet enterprise security needs.

Top 4 bullets (tile-level short bullets):
  - Production-first runtime: GPU-optimized serving, batching, and cache-aware routing
  - Deployment flexibility: Hosted, Dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem)
  - Cost & latency observability: per-token cost breakdown, tracing, rollouts
  - Enterprise controls: KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and compliance options

CTA line examples:
  - "Start with free credits — deploy in minutes."
  - "Contact sales for Dedicated or Private deployments and enterprise SLAs."

Localization notes (for i18n team):
  - Avoid idioms; use neutral phrasing (e.g., "predictable latency" not "snappy performance").
  - Keep numeric examples generic: "units" instead of currency in copy variants for non-USD locales.

Quality checks for copy acceptance:
  - [ ] Plain language: no marketing-only jargon (reviewed by product)
  - [ ] Security/compliance callouts present for Private listing
  - [ ] Accurate feature parity across vendor tiles (AWS/Azure/GCP)
  - [ ] Character counts verified for each vendor tile UI
  - [ ] Linked to up-to-date pricing doc (billing owners sign-off)

Quota & guardrails checklist (these map to the listing metadata + marketplace limits):
- Goals: ensure buyers don’t hit unexpected soft-limits, and Redwood has guardrails to protect multi-tenant capacity and dedicated allocations.

Minimum required metadata for GTM integration: (marketplace ops to populate)
  - Billing SKU visible name (string) — e.g., "redwood.inference.hosted.token"
  - SKU unit (tokens/1000, model-hour, request)
  - Base plan limits (free tier credits or trial units)
  - Reserved capacity mapping (if partner selects Dedicated)
  - Region coverage list (NA / EU / APAC)

Draft operational guardrails (preflight):
  - [ ] Per-account rate limit: default 200 rps; burst 400 rps for approved enterprise tenants
  - [ ] Token-per-minute cap: default 2,000,000 tokens/min per account (adjustable via committed capacity)
  - [ ] Concurrent KV sessions (long-running chat sessions) capped at 500 per account unless Dedicated purchase exists
  - [ ] Auto-fallback policy: if preferred model unavailable, route to certified variant (configurable TTL = 120s)
  - [ ] Maximum request size: 8,000 tokens for Hosted; Dedicated/Private can request exceptions via SOW

Billing & SKU mapping notes (work with finance and marketplace billing team):
  - We prefer per-token billing on hosted API listings. Marketplace SKUs should map to the same unit definitions we use internally to avoid reconciliation drift.
  - For Dedicated offerings, list a monthly reserved SKU with a single "commit-level" attribute and optional burst credits SKU for short-term overages.
  - Trial offer mechanics: free credits flow in as a promotional SKU visible on the marketplace tile. Specify expiration window (e.g., 90 days).

Security/compliance copy snippet (for vendor tile and detail pages):
  "Supports enterprise-grade controls: network isolation (VPC peering for Private deployments), key management integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault), and audit logging for requests and admin actions."

Acceptance criteria for integration QA (ops + engineering):
  - [ ] Tile copy matches approved short/long variants and has vendor character-count sign-off
  - [ ] SKU definitions exist in billing system and map to internal pricing docs
  - [ ] Rate limits and quota metadata are enforceable via the control plane API (test suite green)
  - [ ] Trial credits provision and expire as expected (integration test pass)
  - [ ] Security snippet links to the canonical compliance page (confluence link updated)

Open questions / decisions required (please comment inline):
  - How do we show Dedicated capacity latency SLA on the tile without promising specific p95 numbers per region? (Legal/ops input needed)
  - Do we surface per-model token costs in the tile, or keep pricing to per-token average and leave detailed breakdown in the pricing page? (Finance prefers single SKU to simplify marketplace billing)
  - What is the default auto-fallback model family for EU region? Product to recommend certified variants.

Rollout plan (high level):
  - Week 1: finalize short/long copy + security snippet (Priya)
  - Week 2: marketplace ops create draft tile in each vendor portal + smoke tests (Liam)
  - Week 3: billing SKU creation & reconciliation testing with finance (Marcus)
  - Week 4: partner engineering integration tests (Sofia) and go/no-go

Notes / references:
  - Internal QA suite: github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-integration/tests (PR linked above)
  - Related confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MKT/marketplace-onboarding
  - Slack threads: #marketplace-ops, #partner-launches

TODOs (short):
  - [ ] Product to confirm recommended model-family fallback list (product-ticket: JIRA-3821)
  - [ ] Finance to confirm per-token SKU granularity and trial credit expiry policy
  - [ ] Localization team to provide character-count trimming suggestions for JP/KR tiles

Quick draft examples for vendor tile fields (vendor-specific editing required):
  - Tile title (<= 80 chars): Redwood Inference — production LLM inference (hosted & private)
  - Short subtitle: Predictable latency, cost controls, and enterprise observability
  - Tagline (for search tags): inference, llm, gpu, mlops, enterprise, latency

Feedback welcome — please add comments inline or ping me in #marketplace-ops.

-- Priya
